style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The missionary psalm -- the song David gave the choir the day the ark came to Zion (1 Chronicles 16), rewritten for the whole planet. Its commands sweep outward in rings: sing a new song, all the earth; proclaim His salvation day after day like fresh news; declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples -- Israel's private hymnal ordered to go global. The theology under the mission is stated without apology: all the gods of the peoples are elilim, worthless nothings, but the LORD made the heavens -- one Maker, therefore one message for every nation. The center is a summons to the world's families to give back what has always been His: glory and strength ascribed, offerings carried into His courts, worship in the beauty of holiness. Verse 10 is the sentence the church has carried to every continent: say among the nations, 'The LORD reigns!' And the psalm ends with creation itself joining the choir -- heavens glad, earth rejoicing, sea thundering, fields exulting, every tree of the forest singing -- because He comes, He comes to judge the earth with righteousness and the peoples with His faithfulness. Judgment here is not the dirge; it is the good news the whole cosmos is tuning up for.

1.text: Sing to the LORD a song that is new! Sing to the LORD, all you earth!
1.amp: O sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH] a new [chadash] song [shir]: sing unto the LORD, all the earth [eretz].
1.notes: The shir chadash (H7892, H2319) of Psalm 40:3, now commissioned planet-wide: kol ha-eretz drafted into the choir. New mercies keep demanding new music -- and the triple 'sing' of verses 1-2 sets the tempo of insistence.

2.text: Sing to the LORD and bless His name; herald the good news of His salvation day after day.
2.amp: Sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH], bless [barak] His name [shem]; show forth [basar -- herald as good news] His salvation [yeshuah] from day [yom] to day.
2.notes: basar (H1319) is the gospel-verb, the herald's word: His yeshuah (H3444) announced yom to yom like a bulletin that never goes stale. Evangelism is here a daily periodical, not an annual event.

3.text: Recount His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.
3.amp: Declare [saphar -- recount] His glory [kabod] among the heathen [goy -- the nations], His wonders [pala] among all people [am].
3.notes: The missionary charter in one verse: saphar (H5608), the storyteller's verb, aimed at the goyim -- the kabod and the pala-works (H6381) carried outside Israel's borders. What Psalm 19 says the heavens do wordlessly, God's people are to do with words.

4.text: For the LORD is great, and worthy of the greatest praise; He is to be feared above all that are called gods.
4.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] is great [gadol], and greatly [meod] to be praised [halal]: He is to be feared [yare] above all gods [elohim].
4.notes: The mission's warrant: gadol (H1419) demanding praise scaled meod (H3966) to match. 'Above all elohim' concedes nothing to the rivals -- verse 5 is about to audit their portfolios.

5.text: For every god of the peoples is a worthless idol, but the LORD made the heavens.
5.amp: For all the gods [elohim] of the nations [am] are idols [elil -- worthless things, nothings]: but the LORD [YHWH] made [asah] the heavens [shamayim].
5.notes: The Hebrew puns with a hammer: the elohim of the peoples are elilim (H457) -- 'godlets', nothings, the word built to sound like a deflated elohim. One clause settles the comparison: YHWH asah shamayim -- the rivals are manufactured; He manufactures.

6.text: Splendor and majesty go before His face; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary.
6.amp: Honour [hod -- splendor] and majesty [hadar] are before [panim] Him: strength [oz] and beauty [tipheret] are in His sanctuary [miqdash].
6.notes: The court of the true King: hod and hadar (H1935, H1926) as the attendants before His face, oz and tipheret (H5797, H8597) as the furnishings of His miqdash. Where the idols have nothing, He has an entourage of attributes.

7.text: Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples -- ascribe glory and strength to the LORD!
7.amp: Give [yahab -- ascribe] unto the LORD [YHWH], O ye kindreds [mishpachah -- families] of the people [am], give unto the LORD glory [kabod] and strength [oz].
7.notes: yahab (H3051), the ascribing-verb of Psalm 29, re-addressed: there the summons went to angels, here to the mishpechot (H4940) of the peoples -- the same families promised blessing in Abraham (cf. Genesis 12:3) now summoned to bring the kabod back where it belongs.

8.text: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name; carry an offering and come into His courts.
8.amp: Give [yahab] unto the LORD [YHWH] the glory ['of his name', kabod shem, the KJV margin] due unto His name: bring [nasa] an offering [minchah], and come [bo] into His courts [chatser].
8.notes: kabod shemo: glory measured by the Name it answers to -- praise sized to the Owner. And the nations arrive not as tourists but as worshipers: minchah (H4503) in hand, through the chatser (H2691) gates -- Isaiah's vision of the peoples streaming in, sung in advance (cf. Isaiah 2:2-3; Malachi 1:11).

9.text: Bow down and worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness; writhe in awe before Him, all the earth.
9.amp: O worship [shachah -- bow down, prostrate] the LORD [YHWH] in the beauty [hadarah] of holiness ['in the glorious sanctuary', qodesh, the KJV margin]: fear [chul -- tremble, writhe] before [panim] Him, all the earth [eretz].
9.notes: hadrat qodesh (H1927, H6944): holiness itself as the vestment worship wears. The fear-verb is startling -- chul (H2342), the writhing of childbirth and of Psalm 90:2's birthing mountains: awe that moves the whole body, commanded of the whole eretz.

10.text: Say among the nations: 'The LORD reigns!' Yes, the world stands firm, never to be shaken; He will judge the peoples with straight equity.
10.amp: Say [amar] among the heathen [goy] that the LORD [YHWH] reigns [malak]: the world [tebel] also shall be established [kun] that it shall not be moved [mot]: He shall judge [din] the people [am] righteously [meshar -- with equity].
10.notes: The psalm's headline and the church's oldest missionary sentence: YHWH malak (H4427) -- the LORD reigns -- said AMONG the goyim, in rebel territory. The reign steadies the planet (kun, H3559, against mot, H4131) and guarantees the bench: din be-mesharim (H1777, H4339), judgment running straight.

11.text: Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea thunder, and everything that fills it.
11.amp: Let the heavens [shamayim] rejoice [samach], and let the earth [eretz] be glad [gil]; let the sea [yam] roar [raam -- thunder], and the fulness [melo] thereof.
11.notes: Creation's choir warms up section by section: shamayim on samach, eretz on gil, and the yam assigned its natural part -- raam (H7481), thunder. The melo (H4393), everything that fills it, from Psalm 24:1: the Owner is coming, and the property is glad.

12.text: Let the open field exult, and all that lives in it; then all the trees of the forest will sing out for joy
12.amp: Let the field [sadeh] be joyful [alaz -- exult triumphantly], and all that is therein: then shall all the trees [ets] of the wood [yaar] rejoice [ranan -- ring out]
12.notes: alaz (H5937) is triumphant exultation, granted to farmland -- and then the forest: every ets (H6086) of the yaar singing ranan (H7442). Isaiah heard the same trees clapping (cf. Isaiah 55:12); Paul heard the whole creation groaning FOR this very day (cf. Romans 8:19-22).

13.text: before the LORD -- for He is coming, He is coming to judge the earth! He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples by His faithfulness.
13.amp: Before [panim] the LORD [YHWH]: for He comes [bo], for He comes to judge [shaphat] the earth [eretz]: He shall judge the world [tebel] with righteousness [tsedek], and the people [am] with His truth [emunah].
13.notes: The doubled ki va, ki va -- 'for He comes, for He comes' -- creation's own advent bell. And the astonishment of the psalm: the coming JUDGMENT is what everything sings about, because shaphat (H8199) by tsedek and emunah (H6664, H530) means every crooked thing finally set straight. The dread day for rebellion is coronation day for the cosmos (cf. Acts 17:31; Revelation 19:11).
